title: Remote Control Functional Design Meeting
summary: The team reviewed requirements and discussed the functional design and market positioning for the new remote control. They agreed to target young professionals aged 15 to 35 and keep the initial product scope limited to standard television functions rather than complex home-entertainment systems. Basic controls like power, volume, channel changing, numeric input, and mute will be prioritized, while advanced features may be grouped or concealed. Following lunch, each team member will proceed with their respective component, interface, and market research tasks.
topics: Core versus advanced remote control features
Categorization of controls into audio, video, and device
decisions: The remote control will only operate television sets, omitting Teletext, VCR, and DVD functionality to reduce complexity and time-to-market.
The target demographic is defined as young professionals in the 15 to 35 age group.
Core functional controls will include power, channel up/down, volume up/down, direct numeric channel selection, and mute.
The remote will utilize standard infrared transmission rather than advanced alternatives for this stage.
The device will use regular disposable batteries rather than a rechargeable docking cradle to minimize cost and complexity.
Controls will be categorized into three groups: audio controls, video controls, and general device functions.
